recommendation: Keep the audit commit. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed; future v2-0203/JHN wording changes should go through THO terminology governance rather than editing core ValueSet membership.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core M&M STU3 request to remove "(Canada)" from JHN because the identifier type is not Canada-specific; Jira records harmonization approval.
initial_application: No FHIR source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-17659 was found. The adjacent FHIR-13972 work added code JHN to source/terminologies/valueset-identifier-type.xml in c3b2e501fb466020064156d469506929efd94fa5, while the older R4 package still shows the stale display "Jurisdictional health number (Canada)".
additional_context: Current core does not define the v2-0203/JHN display; it includes JHN by code in the Identifier Type Codes ValueSet and relies on http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v2-0203. Local current THO packages hl7.terminology.r5#5.3.0 and hl7.terminology#4.0.0 define JHN as "Jurisdictional health number", while the old R4 core package shows the historical Canada-specific display. FHIR-13972 is already represented on the combined branch by 78b4ea3195d42faccac7b2731dad63fbd8e45b91.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because current core has no stale JHN "(Canada)" display to remove and the current terminology source of truth already reflects the approved wording.

related_jiras.note: Added JHN to the Identifier Type Codes ValueSet and is already audited on the combined branch, so it was not duplicated here.
Withdrawn UTG proposal referenced JHN as already present while requesting JPID; it did not change JHN or supersede FHIR-17659.
Later no-change request to add another v2-0203 code confirms the ValueSet is an extensible selected subset, not the place to redefine v2-0203 displays.
